precepts.text: Elias was covered with a whirlwind, and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: he was not moved with the presence of any prince, and no word could overcome him. Men, study: when you are out in the street, there should be no word that can confound you. We should not hear men teaching who cannot explain basic scriptures. We are going up against, for the most part, Christians, and they do not know the Bible. We should know who we are and how to explain it: Galatians 3, Ephesians 2:11-16; this is elementary. When the spirit of God is on you, no word should be able to overcome you.
precepts.point: Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine. But Peter, standing up with the eleven, said, these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day. But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel: in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. Prophesy about what? The gathering of the twelve tribes of Israel; teaching the people who they are. The masses did not know; it was the job of the priests and the prophets to teach the people. But in the last days God is raising the message back up, and we are going out to raise our people back up and show them they are not Arabs and Muslims and African Americans or whatever label was put on them: we are the children of Israel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The Holy Ghost came at Pentecost as a rushing mighty wind. Sirach tells of another man covered by the wind: “Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: whilst he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.”

Look what it says next: “No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied.” While the spirit of God was on him, no word could overcome him.

Men, study. When you are out in the street, there should be no word that can confound you. We should not be hearing men teaching who cannot explain basic scriptures. We are going up against, for the most part, Christians, and they don't know the Bible. We should know who we are and how to explain it: Galatians 3, Ephesians 2:11-16. This is very elementary.

When the spirit of God is on you, no word should be able to overcome you. That is what filled the apostles at Pentecost, and that is what should fill the men who go out to teach today.

precepts.text: This is the book of the commandments of God and the law that endureth forever; all they that keep it shall come to life. O Israel, happy are we, for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Sirach ends the praise of Elias and Eliseus with the people after them: “Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” So what is pleasing to God? Baruch answers it: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

Then: “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.” The things pleasing to God are his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Sirach says some did that which was pleasing to God, it means some did the laws of God, and the rest multiplied sins.

That ties back to verse 10, where Elias was “ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That is our job, before it breaks forth, before the decree brings forth and the fierce anger of God comes, as Zephaniah 3 says: to turn our people back to God.

What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws first, and then become the prophets that lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders.

moments.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp. Elias is Elijah the prophet. And his word burned like a lamp, literally and spiritually.
He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number. That is the literal fire that came down from heaven.
By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire.
O Elias, how wast thou honoured in thy wondrous deeds! and who may glory like unto thee!

For Ezekias had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the ways of David his father, as Esay the prophet, who was great and faithful in his vision, had commanded him. So he is talking about Hezekiah as king, and Isaiah the prophet that was with him, who was great and faithful in his vision.

In his time the sun went backward, and he lengthened the king's life. He saw by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Sion. He shewed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things or ever they came.

So that is what a true prophet does. Comfort the people that mourn, and explain to them the secret things. There is no ministry like what we are doing here, where we are going into the Bible and showing you secret things while the world is falling apart.

Elias stood up as fire and his word burned like a lamp. He was ordained for reproofs in their times to pacify the wrath of the Lord's judgment before it broke forth into fury, to turn the heart of the father to the son and restore the tribes of Jacob. That is our job: turn the people back to God before the decree brings forth.
